Maya R: Heads-up — legal asked if our audit export can filter by "actor identity" for canned exports (CSV/NDJSON) and also support a pseudonymized mode for GDPR requests. Anyone already owning this UX/API?
Jia Chen: We have actor_id + actor_type in the event shape already. The question is whether to expose both in the download and how to let customers toggle masking.
Rowan Patel: For console filtering, do we mean a simple search by actor email/name, or role-based filters (service account vs user) + ability to exclude system actors?
Maya R: All of the above. They want: by-actor filters, show "who" in the console, but exported files must be able to mask PII unless the user has export permission.
Priya K: From telemetry perspective, we track actor_id -> org mapping. We could do: export columns = [timestamp, action, resource, actor_display, actor_id]. Add export flag `mask_actors=true|false`.
Jia Chen: Masking implementation options: 1) on-the-fly pseudonymization (hash with per-org salt), 2) return truncated display (first+last initial), 3) fully remove actor fields. Which is preferred?
Maya R: Legal prefers option 1 so we can still link events inside the org without revealing email. Hashing with salt looks good. Need rollover plan for salts.
Rowan Patel: UX question — when mask_actors=true, show a warning banner in console: "Actors masked in export" and a tooltip explaining hash semantics. Also allow admins to download the unmasked version if they have `exports:unmask` permission.
Jia Chen: On the API side, propose query param `mask_actors=1` and header `X-Export-Mode: pseudonymize|remove|raw`. For streaming exports, masking needs to be applied as we serialize. Should be cheap.
Priya K: Note: logs that contain actor identifiers in nested metadata (e.g., policy.change.author) — we need a walker to apply masking everywhere, not just top-level actor fields. This will affect performance, especially for NDJSON big exports.
Maya R: Good catch. Let's identify canonical actor fields and add a fast-path that only masks those by default, with an optional deep-mask flag for compliance.
Jia Chen: Example CSV header suggestion: `ts,action,resource,actor_display,actor_id,actor_type,details` and when masked `actor_display` = `redacted_h_<hash>`, `actor_id` = `redacted_h_<hash>`. Keep the same hash for the same actor within export.
Rowan Patel: For the console filters, searching by actor should match both redacted and raw names for admins. For users without export permissions, search should not reveal PII in exported results.
Maya R: Who can pick this up? I'll scope an RFC with API shape, permission matrix, and UX banners. Need an implementation owner for backend masking walk and for export job changes.
Priya K: I can take telemetry/contract changes and add tests for performance impacts.
audit-export-bot: Export job queued #78912 (mask_actors=1) by maya.r — ETA ~2m.
Jia Chen: I'll take the backend masking worker. Will prototype hash-with-salt + per-org rotation config.
Maya R: Awesome. Let's sync briefly after prototype. Thanks :thumbsup:
Rowan Patel: Quick note — add a changelog entry and a console flag so beta orgs can opt-in before we flip default.
Maya R: Yep, include rollout plan and migration notes.
Priya K: I'll add perf dashboard: export duration, CPU for deep-mask, and bytes/sec.
Jia Chen: Filing a small follow-up: edge-case for service accounts that rotate IDs — hashing must be stable across rotations or we need a mapping table.
Maya R: Add that to RFC. Meeting if needed tomorrow.
Rowan Patel: SG — thanks everyone.
